nodes.description: Heterozygous AFG3L2 missense variants clustered in the ATPase domain reduce m-AAA protease function and alter OPA1 processing in patient fibroblasts, a mechanism distinct from the SCA28 proteolytic-domain variants. This is the dominant, optic-atrophy-predominant arm of the spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: ATPase Domain AFG3L2 Mutations Alter OPA1 Processing and Cause Optic Neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: All the DOA-associated AFG3L2 mutations were clustered in the ATPase domain, whereas SCA28-associated mutations mostly affect the proteolytic domain.

nodes.description: Biallelic hypomorphic (e.g. p.Tyr616Cys) and/or null AFG3L2 genotypes severely reduce m-AAA protease activity and complex assembly, producing the recessive SPAX5 phenotype. The hypomorphic Y616C product shows impaired oligomerization with itself and, more so, with paraplegin.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies homozygous AFG3L2 mutations in a spastic ataxia-neuropathy syndrome linked to mitochondrial m-AAA proteases.
evidence.snippet: the formation of AFG3L2(Y616C) complexes was impaired, both with itself and to a greater extent with paraplegin.

nodes.description: Heterozygous AFG3L2 variants, mostly affecting the proteolytic domain, cause SCA28. The cited source (PMID:22022284) describes them as loss-of-function variants.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies homozygous AFG3L2 mutations in a spastic ataxia-neuropathy syndrome linked to mitochondrial m-AAA proteases.
evidence.snippet: Heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in AFG3L2 cause autosomal-dominant spinocerebellar ataxia type 28 (SCA28), a disorder whose phenotype is strikingly different from that of our patients.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of Function of AFG3L2 Leading to Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy.
evidence.snippet: Compared with spastic ataxia 5-usually involving null-missense or missense-missense genotypes-DEE predominantly features null-null combinations.

evidence.reference_title: ATPase Domain AFG3L2 Mutations Alter OPA1 Processing and Cause Optic Neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Half of cases were familial with a dominant inheritance, whereas the others were sporadic, including de novo mutations.

evidence.reference_title: ATPase Domain AFG3L2 Mutations Alter OPA1 Processing and Cause Optic Neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Twelve cases (4%) were found to carry novel variants in AFG3L2, a gene that has been associated with autosomal dominant spinocerebellar ataxia 28 (SCA28).

evidence.reference_title: AFG3L2-Related Neurologic Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Ophthalmologic findings are optic nerve pallor and highly reduced retinal nerve fiber layer on optical coherence tomography.

nodes.description: Homozygous Afg3l2-deficient mice show impaired axonal development, delayed myelination, poor axonal radial growth and death by about postnatal day 16, modelling the severe biallelic neurologic phenotype; Purkinje-neuron rescue by integrated-stress-response potentiation has been shown in this background.
Cerebellar ataxia is the core feature of SCA28 and of the biallelic spastic-ataxia phenotypes.

evidence.reference_title: AFG3L2-Related Neurologic Disorders.
evidence.snippet: a cerebellar syndrome manifesting initially as very slowly progressive gait and limb ataxia resulting in incoordination and balance problems.

evidence.reference_title: AFG3L2-Related Neurologic Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Optic atrophy type 12 (OPA12) manifests as decreased visual acuity (variable but frequently ranging from 0.2/10 to 2/10), photophobia, and impaired color vision.

evidence.reference_title: AFG3L2-Related Neurologic Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Less frequently, ptosis/ophthalmoplegia, dysarthria, or upper-limb incoordination may occur as the initial finding.

nodes.description: Loss of AFG3L2 function leads to overactivation of the stress-sensitive protease OMA1, which over-processes the fusion GTPase OPA1 to its short, fission-promoting isoforms, fragmenting the mitochondrial network and disturbing mitochondrial distribution in neuronal axons and dendrites. In OPA12 fibroblasts this overprocessing is the proposed basis of the optic-nerve phenotype.
nodes.id: Dysregulated OPA1 Processing and Mitochondrial Fragmentation

evidence.reference_title: ATPase Domain AFG3L2 Mutations Alter OPA1 Processing and Cause Optic Neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Patients' fibroblasts showed abnormal OPA1 processing, with accumulation of the fission-inducing short forms leading to mitochondrial network fragmentation, not observed in SCA28 patients' cells.

evidence.reference_title: AFG3L2-Related Neurologic Disorders.
evidence.snippet: a cerebellar syndrome manifesting initially as very slowly progressive gait and limb ataxia resulting in incoordination and balance problems.

nodes.description: AFG3L2 is the ATP-dependent metallopeptidase subunit of the m-AAA protease of the inner mitochondrial membrane, acting as a homo-oligomer or as a hetero-oligomer with paraplegin (SPG7). Reduced protease activity impairs degradation of damaged or unassembled mitochondrial proteins and maturation of selected substrates, causing accumulation of mitochondria-encoded proteins.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies homozygous AFG3L2 mutations in a spastic ataxia-neuropathy syndrome linked to mitochondrial m-AAA proteases.
evidence.snippet: AFG3L2 forms either a homo-oligomeric isoenzyme or a hetero-oligomeric complex with paraplegin, a homologous protein mutated in hereditary spastic paraplegia type 7 (SPG7).

nodes.description: Failure to clear unassembled mitochondrial calcium-uniporter regulatory subunits deregulates the MCU channel, causing excessive mitochondrial calcium uptake and susceptibility to calcium-induced neuronal death; shown in AFG3L2 compound-heterozygous patient-derived iPSCs.

evidence.reference_title: Compound heterozygous mutation of AFG3L2 causes autosomal recessive spinocerebellar ataxia through mitochondrial impairment and MICU1 mediated Ca(2+) overload.
evidence.snippet: the reduction of the stability of the AFG3L2 protein, and MCU (mitochondrial calcium uniporter) complex mediated Ca2+ overload.

nodes.description: Mitochondrial proteotoxicity on loss of AFG3L2 activates the OMA1-DELE1-HRI axis, eliciting the integrated stress response (eIF2alpha phosphorylation, ATF4 and downstream targets). This is a compensatory, cytoprotective branch rather than a driver of degeneration: silencing DELE1/HRI impairs SPAX5-fibroblast growth, and pharmacological potentiation of the response rescues cells and model mice.

evidence.reference_title: Sustained OMA1-mediated integrated stress response is beneficial for spastic ataxia type 5.
evidence.snippet: pharmacological potentiation of integrated stress response via Sephin-1, a drug that selectively inhibits the stress-induced eIF2alpha phosphatase GADD34 (encoded by Ppp1r15a), improved cell growth of SPAX5 fibroblasts

evidence.reference_title: Sustained OMA1-mediated integrated stress response is beneficial for spastic ataxia type 5.
evidence.snippet: Sephin-1 treatment in vivo extended the lifespan of Afg3l2-/- mice, improved Purkinje neuron morphology, mitochondrial ultrastructure and respiratory capacity.

nodes.description: Bilateral optic atrophy is the core OPA12 feature; onset is usually in the first two decades and the course is slowly progressive or relatively stable.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of AFG3L2 dominant optic atrophy following reanalysis of clinical exome sequencing.
evidence.snippet: A healthy father and daughter of East African heritage experienced the onset of vision loss in the first decade of life due to optic atrophy.

evidence.reference_title: AFG3L2-Related Neurologic Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Ophthalmologic findings are optic nerve pallor and highly reduced retinal nerve fiber layer on optical coherence tomography.

nodes.description: Peripheral neuropathy is part of the spastic ataxia-neuropathy syndrome in the founding biallelic SPAX5 family.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies homozygous AFG3L2 mutations in a spastic ataxia-neuropathy syndrome linked to mitochondrial m-AAA proteases.
evidence.snippet: We report an early onset spastic ataxia-neuropathy syndrome in two brothers of a consanguineous family characterized clinically by lower extremity spasticity, peripheral neuropathy, ptosis, oculomotor apraxia, dystonia, cerebellar atrophy, and progressive myoclonic epilepsy.

nodes.description: Cerebellar Purkinje cells, corticospinal motor neurons and peripheral axons are especially vulnerable to AFG3L2-dependent mitochondrial failure, producing cerebellar ataxia, dysarthria, spasticity and neuropathy. Purkinje-cell dark degeneration and axonal/myelination defects are reproduced in Afg3l2 mouse models.

evidence.reference_title: The mitochondrial protease AFG3L2 is essential for axonal development.
evidence.snippet: Afg3l2 models display a marked impairment of axonal development with delayed myelination and poor axonal radial growth leading to lethality at P16.

evidence.reference_title: AFG3L2-Related Neurologic Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Optic atrophy type 12 (OPA12) manifests as decreased visual acuity (variable but frequently ranging from 0.2/10 to 2/10), photophobia, and impaired color vision.

nodes.description: Defective mitochondrial proteostasis impairs OPA1 processing, mtDNA maintenance, membrane potential, ATP production and respiratory capacity, a loss-of-function bioenergetic failure demonstrated in patient fibroblasts across the biallelic spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of Function of AFG3L2 Leading to Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy.
evidence.snippet: defective OPA1 processing, decreased mtDNA content, impaired membrane potential and ATP production, fragmented mitochondrial networks, and diminished respiratory capacity, supporting a loss-of-function mechanism.

nodes.description: In retinal ganglion cells and their optic-nerve axons, mitochondrial fragmentation, calcium overload and respiratory failure cause axonal loss, with reduced retinal nerve fiber layer, optic-disc pallor, dyschromatopsia and progressive central visual impairment (the OPA12 phenotype).
nodes.id: Retinal Ganglion Cell and Optic Nerve Degeneration

evidence.snippet: an early onset spastic ataxia-neuropathy syndrome in two brothers of a consanguineous family characterized clinically by lower extremity spasticity, peripheral neuropathy, ptosis, oculomotor apraxia, dystonia, cerebellar atrophy, and progressive myoclonic epilepsy.

nodes.description: Pyramidal signs including spasticity occur in SCA28 with longer disease duration and are a core feature of the biallelic spastic-ataxia phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: AFG3L2-Related Neurologic Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Pyramidal syndrome (increased and brisk reflexes, extensor plantar reflex, and spasticity) is commonly observed in individuals with longer disease duration.

nodes.description: c.1064C>T (NM_006796.3) heterozygous missense; reported as pathogenic in a father-daughter nonsyndromic optic-atrophy family diagnosed by exome reanalysis.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of AFG3L2 dominant optic atrophy following reanalysis of clinical exome sequencing.
evidence.snippet: Reanalysis of the sequencing data revealed an autosomal dominant pathogenic variant in AFG3L2, c.1064C>T (p.Thr355Met), a gene that was recently identified to be associated with non-syndromic optic atrophy.

nodes.description: c.1847G>A (p.Y616C) homozygous missense; the foundational SPAX5 allele, a hypomorphic variant with impaired m-AAA complex oligomerization.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies homozygous AFG3L2 mutations in a spastic ataxia-neuropathy syndrome linked to mitochondrial m-AAA proteases.
evidence.snippet: Whole-exome sequencing identified a homozygous missense mutation (c.1847G>A; p.Y616C) in AFG3L2, encoding a subunit of an m-AAA protease.
